brief: A dog curled asleep on a sagging sofa, rendered as a thermal camera image. Soft airbrushed spray gradients run from indigo and violet on the cool cushions, through magenta, to blazing yellow-white at the dog's belly, nose and paw pads. Hyperreal fur direction is still legible as fine pencil strands drifting through the false colour. A warm handprint ghost fades on the armrest beside it. A small temperature-scale bar and crosshair are drawn in thin white pen at the corner. The image is quiet, intimate and electric.

A steaming bowl of tonkotsu ramen from a slightly elevated angle, in strict black-and-white manga technique. Broth, chashu marbling, a halved soft egg's jammy yolk and nori texture are rendered with hyperreal fidelity using layered dot and line screentones. The tones are cut sharply along forms, with white highlights scratched out. Steam rises in clean pen-outlined wisps against a dense cross-hatched counter. Radiating speed lines burst from the bowl as if it has just arrived. Dynamic diagonal framing, high contrast, pure ink. It should feel eager and cinematic.

A tight crop of a school bus side panel, read as a hard-edge painting. Vast razor-clean fields of chrome yellow are cut by two flat black bands, with every edge taped-sharp and no gradients in the big planes. The hyperrealism lives entirely in small zones: the riveted seam, a dented corner and a reflected sliver of sky and telephone wire in the window's black glass. These are rendered in fine marker and pen. The composition is mostly abstract geometry, so the viewer only slowly recognises the vehicle.

A tight crop of zebra flank in motion. The stripes are rendered with ikat's feathered, resist-bled edges: each black band frays into the cream ground in jagged, stepped flares, as if the dye had crept along warp threads. Charcoal mass and dry-dragged watercolour build this effect. Within the softness, individual hairs, a scar and a fly on the shoulder are hyperreal and needle-sharp. The ground is warm ivory with a faint indigo shadow undertone. The stripes run on a diagonal sweep across the whole sheet, and there is no horizon.

An overhead view of a shallow tiled fountain basin with copper and nickel coins resting under still, clear water. The tile floor is drawn as an interlocking girih strapwork of ten-pointed stars and bow-tie pentagons in crisp sepia pen, filled with glassy watercolour glazes of lapis, turquoise and saffron. The water refracts and bends the geometry, kinking the straps at each ripple. Each coin is rendered in hyperreal detail, with worn milled edges and green patina. The strict lattice meets photographic caustics, and pale light threads cross the tiles.

A tumbled heap of twist-wrapped hard candies fills the frame edge to edge. Each sweet is a stack of transparent watercolour layers: raspberry, lime and butterscotch cores seen through crinkled film, with overlaps darkening wherever two wrappers cross. Every crease in the cellophane carries a knife-thin white marker glint and a cool cyan edge reflection. The twisted ends fan out in fine pen hairlines. There is no background, only more candy dissolving into soft colour at the borders. The surface is slick and dazzling and the pigments are pure, with no greys anywhere.

An open bakery box of glazed doughnuts seen from above, sticky sheen and torn sugar crust rendered in perfect detail, but printed as if on a curling thermal till receipt. Everything is made of fine warm-grey pen stipple and dithered dot rows, densest in the shadows of the dough holes. The image fades unevenly toward one edge, as thermal print does when it ages, and faint horizontal banding runs across it. A narrow vertical strip format holds the image, with tiny ruled lines and a torn serrated bottom edge. The palette is pale ivory with a faint pink-grey tint, cheap and ghostly.

A rack of old copper saucepans hanging in a farmhouse kitchen, their warm salmon-pink metal blooming with crusts of verdigris. Granulating watercolour does the work. Wet-in-wet blossoms of malachite, viridian and powdery Paris green spread into burnished copper glazes, with hard backrun edges imitating oxidation tide lines. A fine spray speckle adds pitted texture. Polished patches reflect a blurred window in hot orange. Riveted handles and dents are drawn with crisp pencil. The cluster overlaps densely toward the top edge, and the palette pivots on the complementary clash of copper and green.

A sprinter's spiked shoe and taut calf caught mid-stride, drawn entirely in fine iron-oxide red-brown pen on a warm cream slip ground, the way Moche painters drew runners on stirrup-spout vessels. Hyperrealism comes from line alone. Hundreds of hair-thin parallel strokes model the tendon, the mesh of the shoe and the stitched heel tab, with no tone wash at all. The composition wraps around an implied curved vessel surface, so the edges bend and foreshorten. Small dotted borders and a band of stylised track lines frame the scene. The look is austere and two-tone, intensely detailed yet calligraphic.

A round rock tide pool seen straight down, framed like a petri dish, its rim a crisp ring of wet granite. Inside, sea anemones, barnacle clusters and pink coralline crusts spread in colonies. They are painted with watercolour blooms in agar amber, carmine, mustard and olive that bleed at the edges, then sharpened with stippled pen dots and fine tentacle lines. Colonies cluster unevenly and touch, and the clear water carries faint surface reflections. The circle sits on a dark slate field with one corner of a hand holding it, clinical and alive.

A halved papaya mirrored into a radial, eightfold Hawaiian quilt appliqué motif in turkey red on a bleached cotton field. Inside each cut-fabric silhouette the fruit is painted with hyperreal wet glazes of coral, tangerine and glossy black seed clusters, each seed holding a pinprick highlight. Around the motif, concentric echo-quilting lines ripple outward in soft graphite, following every contour like waves around an island. Tiny pencil stitches pucker the edges. Symmetry is strict and the colour is limited to two fabric tones plus the luscious fruit flesh within them.

An ice-cold soda can dripping condensation on a vending-machine tray, rendered hyperreal through a strict grid of chunky square marker pixels. The palette is limited to a console-style set: cherry red, two silvers, a cyan, a deep navy and white. Despite the coarse grid, careful dithering produces the cylinder's curve, the pull-tab glint and each bead of water running down the aluminium. Hard stepped edges have no anti-aliasing. The whole image sits slightly off-centre on a dark navy field, with a faint scanline rhythm of slightly lighter rows.

A pneumatic jackhammer biting into asphalt, rendered with forensic precision but broken into the jagged wedges of Vorticism. The steel shaft, the worker's gloved knuckles and the flying chips of tarmac are drawn in hard graphite and stiff pen hatching, with every scuff and oil smear exact. Behind them, flat watercolour shards of slate grey, burnt sienna and acid yellow ochre rake diagonally across the sheet like shrapnel. Edges are knife-sharp and the hatching changes direction at each plane. There is no soft gradient and no resting horizontal anywhere, only clattering kinetic geometry around a photographically real tool.

The corner of a black lacquered grand piano lid, so glossy it becomes a volcanic-glass mirror holding a warped reflection of a window and a pianist's hands. Built from deep layered charcoal mass in ivory black and blue-black, with lifted, razor-thin highlights that break along conchoidal curves like fractured obsidian. Reflections are crisp near the edge and dissolve into velvety darkness. Tiny dust motes and fingerprint smudges sit on the surface. The composition is heavily cropped and asymmetric, almost entirely black, with one cold white glint carrying the drama.

A steam locomotive's driving wheel and connecting rod, hyperreal down to the rivets and grease, rendered as a frame of tinted silent film. The whole image is monochrome in a toned Prussian cyan, built from layered charcoal with lifted steam plumes. Fine vertical scratches, dust specks and a flickering uneven vignette darken the corners. A thin black frame line and a sliver of the sprocket edge run along one side. Tonal range is compressed and slightly bleached in the highlights, with a dreamy, mechanical, nostalgic mood.

A symmetrical New Year composition: two fat koi arching toward each other above a heaped porcelain bowl of glossy mandarins with leaves still attached. Each scale, water droplet and dimpled rind is rendered in hyperreal detail. The palette is festive nianhua: vermilion, peach pink, emerald, lemon yellow and lacquer black, saturated and opaque. Firm black pen contours echo woodblock key lines, filled with dense marker colour and modelled with subtle gradations. The background is a flat cinnabar red with no horizon. The mood is auspicious, abundant and frankly cheerful, with everything centred and mirrored.

A swimmer bursting up out of a turquoise pool, water sheeting off the cheekbones and goggles, built like a rotoscoped frame. Wobbling black marker contours are traced over flat, slightly misregistered watercolour fills of cerulean, pale flesh pink and chlorine green. The hyperreal detail lives in the obsessive density of the traced lines: every droplet, every strand of wet hair, every refraction ripple gets its own trembling outline. A faint second ghost contour, offset from the first, hints at the previous frame. The surface is luminous and cartoon-flat yet uncannily accurate.

A polished slab of labradorite resting on dark green jeweller's felt beside a brass loupe, rendered with gemological precision. Most of the stone is a dull smoky grey, but across one band it flashes into electric peacock blue, then gold and a thin edge of copper, exactly where light catches the internal lamellae. Watercolour glazes are laid in transparent overlapping veils so the flashes glow from within, and fine pen lines trace the striated crystal cleavage. The felt is a soft charcoal-mass texture. The angle is low and raking, and the flash rewards close looking.

Seen through a perfect circular moon gate in a whitewashed garden wall, a woman in an indigo cotton tunic sweeps fallen ginkgo leaves on grey flagstones. The wall in the foreground is rendered in meticulous pencil: hairline plaster cracks, lime streaks and the worn edge of the round opening. Beyond the gate, the garden is luminous, wet-layered watercolour in ginkgo gold, moss green and stone grey, sharp yet softer than the frame. The circle sits off-centre, and most of the sheet is the pale wall. The mood is still and contemplative.

Directly overhead, a rice farmer's conical straw hat fills the sheet, each woven ring stepping down like terraced paddies. Fine pencil contour lines trace every plaited band, frayed straw end and sweat-darkened patch with absolute precision. Between the rings, thin translucent watercolour in pale jade, wet-mud umber and reflected-sky silver suggests flooded steps holding water. The edges of the hat break into blurred glimpses of green seedling rows below. The rhythm is concentric, layered and patient, and the palette is earthy and cool.
